title: Coherent evaluation from a dinatural section of an arbitrary functor family
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent transformations and cones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the space category $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], coherent Hom bifunctors of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], and $\operatorname{Tw}(C)$ with projection $(s,t)$ of [lem-coef-twisted-arrow-left-fibration]. Let $C$ be a $\mathcal V$-small quasicategory and put $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$, formed in a containing universe. Use the $\mathcal V$-small models for its mapping spaces supplied by [lem-coef-coherent-end-twisted-arrow-formula]. Let $A:C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal F$ be any coherent functor. Write $B_A:C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$ for the coherent evaluation bifunctor $B_A(a,b)=A(a)(b)$. Suppose given a coherent section, meaning a coherent transformation
$$\xi:\Delta_{\operatorname{Tw}(C)}*\longrightarrow B_A\circ(s,t).$$
Write $\xi_a\in A(a)(a)$ for its value at $1_a$. Define coherent functors on $C\times\mathcal F$ by
$$M_A(a,Q)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F}(A(a),Q),\qquad E(a,Q)=Q(a).$$
There is a coherent transformation $e_\xi:M_A\to E$ whose component is the whole-space evaluation map $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_a(\xi_a)$. In particular, for $u:a\to b$, its naturality homotopy identifies $e_{\xi,b,Q}(\alpha\circ A(u))$ with $Q(u)(e_{\xi,a,Q}(\alpha))$; for $v:Q\to Q'$ it identifies $e_{\xi,a,Q'}(v\circ\alpha)$ with $v_a(e_{\xi,a,Q}(\alpha))$. These homotopies are the restrictions of the single coherent transformation, with all higher mixed simplices retained. The construction is coherent also in simplicial families of $(A,\xi)$: a coherent family of such data gives the corresponding family of transformations, commuting with restriction of its parameter simplicial set. Empty $C$ is allowed. No representability hypothesis on $A$ and no equivalence assertion for $e_\xi$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent-formulated coherent dinatural-section evaluation pairing, extending the fixed-object comparison of Kerodon Notation 8.3.1.2 (03M4) using coherent ends as in Example 8.3.4.22 (03P7). Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, construction (5.8.8.4), printed p.257, is the identity-element specialization. These sources do not state the arbitrary-family assertion verbatim. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copies WANTED. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})=\mathcal F$. Transpose the coherent Hom bifunctor restricted along $A^{\mathrm{op}}$ to obtain a coherent functor $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$ with $R(Q)(a)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(A(a),Q)$. The two contravariances, that of $A$ and that of the first Hom variable, cancel, so $R(Q)$ is covariant on $C$. Its transpose is exactly $M_A$. The local-smallness clause of spatial mapping interchange supplies a coherent Hom bifunctor valued in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, so $R$ really lands in $\mathcal D$. Functor categories used here are quasicategories. Choose $\mathcal V\in\mathcal W$ so that $\mathcal D$ and all the displayed functor categories are small in a further containing universe. Later we apply the coherent-end theorem with value universe $\mathcal W$ and index $\mathcal D$, rather than incorrectly treating $\mathcal D$ as $\mathcal V$-small.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping calculation; agent-written contraction using the existing spatial-interchange and coherent-end statements. Online Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 supplies context, not this argument verbatim.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $P,Q\in\mathcal D$, apply spatial mapping interchange with $K=L=C$, $F=P$ and $W=B_A$. Its $R_Q$ is exactly $R(Q)$, so it gives a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(P,R(Q))\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}}\times C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})}(B_A,T_{P,Q}),\qquad T_{P,Q}(a,b)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}}(P(a),Q(b)).$$
For $\alpha:P\to R(Q)$ the corresponding $\tau$ has whole-space component $\tau_{a,b}(w)(x)=\alpha_a(x)_b(w)$. All hypotheses hold: both indexing categories are $\mathcal V$-small and $B_A$ is the coherent transpose of the given $A$. We use the equivalence on entire transformation spaces, together with its stated coherent naturality in $P,Q$; no pointwise family is being assembled here.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping calculation; agent-written contraction using the existing spatial-interchange and coherent-end statements. Online Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 supplies context, not this argument verbatim.

proof.text:
Restrict $\tau:B_A\to T_{P,Q}$ along $\lambda=(s,t)$ and compose with the given $\xi:\Delta*\to B_A\lambda$. This gives a coherent cone $\tau\lambda\circ\xi:\Delta*\to T_{P,Q}\lambda$. The coherent-end formula for $P,Q:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$, read in the reverse direction, turns this cone into a point of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(P,Q)$. Indeed its limit is the space of cones from $*$, by the mapping-space characterization of a limiting cone and $\operatorname{Map}(*,Z)\simeq Z$. The latter is the point-family theorem with shape $\Delta^0$. Consequently this procedure defines a map
$$\kappa_{P,Q}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(P,R(Q))\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(P,Q).$$
Restriction, composition with $\xi$, and the natural inverse of the end equivalence act on all simplices. Their naturality, and that of Step 2, make $\kappa$ a coherent map of bifunctors on $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal D$, with $P$ contravariant and $Q$ covariant. At the identity-arrow projection of $a$, its formula is $\kappa_{P,Q}(\alpha)_a(x)=\alpha_a(x)_a(\xi_a)$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping calculation; agent-written contraction using the existing spatial-interchange and coherent-end statements. Online Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 supplies context, not this argument verbatim.

proof.text: Now apply the coherent-end theorem with index category $\mathcal D$, target category $\mathcal D$ and smallness universe $\mathcal W$. Both the object set of $\mathcal D$ and its mapping spaces are $\mathcal W$-small, since $C$ and every value of its functors are $\mathcal V$-small and $\mathcal V\in\mathcal W$. Apply it first to $R,R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D$. The identity of $R$ determines a coherent section over $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathcal D)$ of $(Q_0,Q_1)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(R(Q_0),R(Q_1))$. Restrict the coherent map $\kappa$ of Step 3 along $(Q_0,Q_1)\mapsto(R(Q_0),Q_1)$ and apply it to this section. The result is a section of $(Q_0,Q_1)\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(R(Q_0),Q_1)$. Applying the end equivalence to $R,\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ gives a single coherent transformation $\eta:R\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$. Its component at $Q$ is $\kappa_{R(Q),Q}(1_{R(Q)})$. This use of the outer end is what supplies all coherence in $Q$, including the mixed simplices with $C$; no claim of naturality is inferred from isolated edge homotopies.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping calculation; agent-written contraction using the existing spatial-interchange and coherent-end statements. Online Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 supplies context, not this argument verbatim.

proof.text:
Transpose the actual map $\mathcal D\times\Delta^1\to\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ defining $\eta$ to obtain $C\times\mathcal D\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal V}$. This is $e_\xi:M_A\to E$. In Step 3 put $P=R(Q)$ and $\alpha=1_{R(Q)}$. Its component calculation gives
$$e_{\xi,a,Q}(x)=x_a(\xi_a),\qquad x\in\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(A(a),Q).$$
This is a whole-space evaluation map because the interchange formula and both identity-arrow projections are formulas of maps of spaces, not just of vertices. Transposition here is the defining internal-functor adjunction: an $n$-simplex is exactly a map from the product with $\Delta^n$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent mapping calculation; agent-written contraction using the existing spatial-interchange and coherent-end statements. Online Kerodon Example 8.3.4.22 supplies context, not this argument verbatim.

proof.text:
For $u:a\to b$, the two edges in $\operatorname{Tw}(C)$ from $1_a$ and $1_b$ to $u$ give, by the section $\xi$, a homotopy
$$A(a)(u)(\xi_a)\simeq A(u)_b(\xi_b).$$
For $x:A(a)\to Q$, naturality of $x$ and this homotopy give
$$e_{\xi,b,Q}(x\circ A(u))=x_b(A(u)_b(\xi_b))\simeq x_b(A(a)(u)(\xi_a))\simeq Q(u)(x_a(\xi_a)).$$
For $v:Q\to Q'$, the component formula gives $e_{\xi,a,Q'}(v\circ x)\simeq v_a(e_{\xi,a,Q}(x))$ by the composition homotopy. These are restrictions of the transformation already constructed in Steps 4–5, whose end projections and interchange maps retain higher simplices. Thus the displayed homotopies have all higher mixed compatibilities. The same construction applies to a simplicial family of $(A,\xi)$: Step 2 is coherent in the weight $B_A$, Step 3 is composition with the entire section family, and both end equivalences commute with extra parameters and restriction. Taking their natural inverses in these functor categories gives the family of transformations and its restriction compatibilities. If $C$ is empty then $C\times\mathcal D$ is empty and the transformation is unique. If $C$ is nonempty the supplied points $\xi_a$ impose exactly their stated nonemptiness, without any additional representability or equivalence hypothesis.
